title: 15 Easy Dinner Recipes for Two – Quick, Cozy Meals from My Kitchen
metaTitle: 15 Easy Dinner Recipes for Two | Chef Augustin
metaDescription: Discover 15 practical, flavorful dinner recipes scaled perfectly for two people. From 20-minute garlic butter pasta to a small-batch lasagna, each dish minimizes leftovers and cleanup.
excerpt: These 15 dinner recipes for two are built for real weeknights — quick, one-pan whenever possible, and full of the kind of flavor that makes cooking feel like a treat, not a chore.

faq.q: What supplies do I need for these one-pan recipes?
faq.a: Most of these recipes call for a 10- or 12-inch skillet, preferably one that can go from stovetop to oven if needed. A good chef’s knife and a cutting board will handle the prep. Beyond that, you’ll just need basic pots for boiling pasta or rice, a baking sheet for the pot pie or lasagna, and a few mixing bowls. I cook with simple, everyday tools, and these recipes reflect that.

faq.q: Can I adjust these recipes if I’m cooking for one?
faq.a: Absolutely. The portions are designed for two, but halving them is straightforward. For recipes that use a single chicken breast or steak, you can cook one and save the second piece for another meal. For skillet dishes with rice or pasta, you can cut the ingredients in half and reduce the cooking time slightly. The recipe notes often include tips for scaling down.

faq.q: Are there vegetarian options in this list?
faq.a: While the majority of these recipes feature meat or seafood, the stovetop mac and cheese is vegetarian and can be a satisfying main dish when paired with a side salad. You could also adapt the one-pan garlic tomato chicken and rice by swapping the chicken for chickpeas and using vegetable broth. The garlic butter shrimp could be replaced with pan-seared mushrooms for a similar texture.

faq.q: How do I store leftovers for two?
faq.a: I recommend storing leftovers in airtight containers in the fridge. Most of these dishes will keep for up to three days. For recipes with crispy elements like the puff pastry lid on the pot pie, it’s best to reheat in the oven to restore some texture. The chili colorado, lasagna, and chicken skillet dishes often taste even better the next day. I try to portion them into two-serving containers so you have a ready-made lunch.

faq.q: What’s the best way to time multiple components of a dinner?
faq.a: I always read the recipe through first, then gather all my ingredients before I start cooking. Many of these recipes are written to use the same pan in stages, so you’ll sear a protein, set it aside, and build the sauce while the pasta or rice cooks. I’ll often start the side that takes the longest (like rice or roasted vegetables) first, then move to the skillet work. With practice, you’ll find a rhythm that makes the whole meal come together at the same time.

faq.q: Can I make these recipes ahead of time?
faq.a: Several of these dinners work well as make-ahead meals. The chicken enchilada skillet, chili colorado, and lasagna can be assembled or fully cooked the day before and reheated. The garlic butter chicken pasta is best fresh, but you can prep the chicken and measure out ingredients ahead of time. For the salmon orzo, I’d recommend cooking it just before serving, as the orzo can absorb liquid and soften further upon sitting.
